target_customer: Runners, cyclists and triathletes booking events, and event organizers paying a fee to sell entries
problem: Finding and entering endurance races is fragmented across low tech organizer sites.
business_model: Marketplace taking a fee on event entries

founders.name: Sam Browne
founders.background_notes: Described as an endurance runner and cyclist; education not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: RunSignup
competitors.what: Race registration and timing platform for organizers
competitors.traction_then: About 4.34 million participants on platform in 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace search, event data aggregation and checkout; hard part was assembling a reliable event catalogue.

defensibility.rationale: Listings of over 30,000 races and organizer relationships build two sided liquidity, but registration platforms already hold organizers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Registration platforms stayed organizer focused; no evidence found of a copy of the consumer discovery marketplace.

market_need_then: RunSignup reported flat to declining participation in 2018, and TechCrunch says organizers often use low tech platforms, which left discovery fragmented.

identity.logo: Earlier logo had an underscore, retired in 2021 redesign
identity.voice_and_tone: Motivational; positioning line Moments Make Us

branding.brand_signature: Serena Williams, Usain Bolt and Paula Radcliffe as celebrity backers

rebrands.to: Nomad designed identity with Moments Make Us positioning
rebrands.why: Earlier brand lacked personality and cohesion per VP of product design

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity investors and more than 5 million users reported in 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: Motivational name and celebrity backing give recognition, but name is a generic phrase and evidence of brand driven growth is limited.

outcome_analysis: Let's Do This built an endurance events marketplace out of YC Winter 2018, raised a reported 5 million seed and 15 million Series A in 2019 and a 60 million Series B in 2022 with US expansion. It remains active with over 5 million users claimed, so it has scaled, but competing registration platforms and the 2018 flat participation trend leave the path to a large outcome open.
notes: letsdothis.com returned 403 on fetch. Seed amount and date from a Crunchbase News snippet, investors unknown; Series A amount from tech.eu and others (snippets), not opened. Another source says total raised about $31M, vs 5+15+60 recorded, so totals are inconsistent.
